7 انحطّ , quasi-pass. of حَطَّهُ; It was, or became, put down; (S, * TA;) said of [a load, or any other thing from a back;] a camel's saddle; a horse's saddle; (TA;) [&c.] ―
-b2- He, or it, descended; went down, or downwards, or down a declivity; from above to below. (S, * TA.) You say, انحطّ فِى حَدَرٍ [He descended a declivity]. (S and TA in art. حدر, from a trad.) ―
-b3- [(assumed tropical:) He became lowered, or degraded.] ―
-b4- Said of a price: see 1. ―
-b5- Said of a camel: see 1. ―
-b6- Also (assumed tropical:) He, or it, went back, or backward: went away: perished. (TA.) ―
-b7- See also R. Q. 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
